Lithium chloride injection in rats increased radioimmunoreactive plasma glucagon, increased hepatic glycogen phosphorylase activity and decreased hepatic glycogen.
lithium chloride induced a glycogen-depleted liver and that the glycogen-depleted effect was caused by an increase of glucagon secretion.
the intraperitoneal injection, but not intracisternal injection, of lithium chloride increased radioimmuno-assayable glucagon, liver glycogen and liver phosphorylases-a activity in rats.

the study of the effect of lithium on the glycogen metabolism of the liver.
the study of the effects of lithium on the liver and on the plasma levels of glucagon.
the study of the effects of intracranial administration of lithium chloride on the glycogen metabolism of rat liver.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
lithium chloride, when injected intraperitoneally, increases the secretion of glucagons from the alpha cells of the pancreatic islets.
lithium is a potent stimulator of glucagon secretion, which in turn is responsible for the liver glycogen depletion.
the effect of lithium on glycogen depletion in the liver is caused by an increased secretion of glucagon from the A cells of the pancreas.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
lithium chloride induced glycogen depletion of liver is caused by an increased secretion of glucagon.
the lithium induced increase of plasma glucagon is not a direct action on the pancreas.
the lithium induced increase in plasma glucagon is not mediated by the central nervous system.
